investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'Programm & Tickets' page. A single retained <script type=application/ld+json> block on that one page contains a JSON array of 150 full schema.org Event objects (name, startDate, doorTime, endDate, location with full postal address, performer, and an AggregateOffer with price/currency) — no per-event crawling needed at all, matching the same bulk-array JSON-LD pattern already proven for moog-barcelona-01.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official programme page (https://www.tempodrom.de/programm-und-tickets/) immediately exposed a single JSON-LD array of 150 Event objects covering essentially the venue's full upcoming schedule at once, each with startDate/doorTime/endDate/location/performer/offers. No further escalation was needed; Level 1 fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Tempodrom (concert/circus-tent-shaped multi-purpose venue, Möckernstraße, Kreuzberg, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'Tempodrom | Tempodrom - Programm & Tickets' at the venue's own domain tempodrom.de. Every sampled JSON-LD event's own 'location' object directly states name 'Tempodrom Berlin' and a full postal address ('Möckernstr. 10, 10963 Berlin, DE') matching the venue's known Kreuzberg address, and every image asset URL is self-hosted under www.tempodrom.de/site/assets/ — a self-consistent, first-party retained artifact.

site_classification.platform: Custom CMS (no WordPress/wp-content/wp-json signal detected). The programme page embeds a single schema.org Event JSON-LD array covering essentially the venue's entire upcoming schedule in one request, matching the same pattern already proven for moog-barcelona-01.

title.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'name' field, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'startDate' date portion (e.g. '2026-09-01T20:30:00'), stated directly.

time.value: 20:30 (Europe/Berlin, floating local — no explicit UTC offset suffix on 'startDate')
time.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'startDate' time-of-day portion, stated directly (e.g. '2026-09-01T20:30:00'). No timezone offset is appended to this value anywhere in the sampled data — recorded honestly as FLOATING_LOCAL, not upgraded to a UTC instant. A separate 'doorTime' field (e.g. '2026-09-01T18:30:00') is also directly present and distinct from the performance start time.

end.notes: A JSON-LD 'endDate' field is present, but was found — by comparing a single-day event (Baby Keem: startDate '2026-09-01T20:30:00', endDate '2026-09-01', identical calendar day, no time-of-day component) against a genuine multi-day event (Berlin Salsacongress 2026: startDate '2026-08-27', endDate '2026-08-30', a 4-day span) — to represent the last calendar day of a (possibly multi-day) event run, not a performance end-time. Treating it as a proven performance 'end' fact would be a misreading of what this field actually encodes, so it is honestly recorded NOT_PRESENT rather than promoted.

venue_location.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'location.name'/'location.address' fields, stated directly and identically across sampled records.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id is exposed on the Event object itself; each event's own 'url' field is this source's own permanent '/event/{slug}/' page, so the slug is used as source_record_id — the same documented judgement already established for moog-barcelona-01/LAV (ingestion/lav/discovery.mjs).

event_url.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'url' field, stated directly.

price.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'offers' object (an AggregateOffer for this sampled record) directly states 'price'/'lowPrice'/'highPrice'/'priceCurrency'/'availability' — a genuinely complete price field, unlike most other Berlin venues already investigated in this trial (which only expose a 'starting from' text string or no price at all).

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, JSON-LD's own location/address, self-hosted asset URLs).

A CONFIRMED public data path retained: a single request exposing 150 full Event records at once.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own URL-slug permalink, following the documented moog-barcelona-01/LAV precedent.
venue_location and price both additionally PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — this source exposes a genuinely complete price range, unlike most other Berlin venues already investigated in this trial.
recommended_family JSON_LD, this project's own existing, fully generic, already-proven collector family (ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs) — literally zero new code required.
DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence now retained (tests/json-ld-berlin-zero-code-cohort.test.mjs) — gate 9/v1.2 satisfied. Advanced from READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.

NOTE (post-investigation, BEATMAPPED-BERLIN-30-40-VENUE-COLLECTOR-REUSE-TRIAL-01 build phase): this source's own real page emits an unquoted script type attribute (<script type=application/ld+json>), which the EXISTING ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs regex did not originally match at all. Fixed as a small, backward-compatible widening of that existing regex (quotes now optional) rather than a new module — see ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs's own doc comment and tests/json-ld-berlin-zero-code-cohort.test.mjs. Reported honestly in the Berlin trial report as CONFIGURATION_ONLY, not pure zero-code, because existing collector implementation code did change to support this source.

evidence.description: The venue's official 'Programm & Tickets' page — the full raw response was originally 709,889 bytes, dominated by navigation/CSS/image markup carrying no event data; this file retains the page's <title> plus the FULL, UNTRUNCATED <script type=application/ld+json> block verbatim (all 150 Event records, not edited or re-serialized), a bounded, disclosed excerpt per the policy's evidence-boundedness requirement. Because the JSON-LD block itself was copied byte-for-byte (not re-parsed/re-serialized), it remains byte_faithful for that portion; the overall file is marked non-byte-faithful since the surrounding page bytes were dropped.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser); response then truncated to title+JSON-LD only, disclosed in this description

evidence.description: A real, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/json-ld-berlin-zero-code-cohort.test.mjs) re-parsing this investigation's own retained fixture via the EXISTING generic collector family and reproducing the exact claimed field values deterministically.
